claims.text: A hybrid DFT+ML approach will predict the thermal conductivity of bulk HfNbTaTiZr more accurately than conventional analytical models based on perfect, defect-free crystals.
The proposed approach is applicable to HfNbTaTiZr specimens containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
Bulk HfNbTaTiZr produced under typical conditions naturally contains point defects and microstructural disorder.
DFT can provide baseline vibrational and transport properties for HfNbTaTiZr.
An ML model trained on experimental conductivity data can correct the DFT baseline in the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K regimes.
Defect-related scattering and possible quantum-mechanical effects dominate thermal transport in the 0–200 K regime.
Phonon anharmonicity and oxygen-impurity scattering are significant in the 300–1200 K regime.
Variations in defect density modify phonon dispersion and scattering rates in HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxygen produces impurity phases that modify phonon dispersion and scattering rates.
Learning discrepancies between ideal-crystal DFT predictions and measurements on defect-bearing specimens can capture the effects of microstructural imperfections on phonon transport.
Accounting for defects and oxygen content will improve agreement between predicted and measured thermal conductivity.
The hybrid approach may reduce prediction error by approximately 20–40% relative to conventional analytical models.
Perfect-crystal analytical predictions inaccurately represent disorder and impurity-scattering effects on thermal conductivity.
The proposed approach is expected to be valid within 0–200 K and 300–1200 K for specimens containing up to approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
The accuracy of the approach outside the specified temperature windows or above approximately 1 wt.% oxygen is unverified.
The magnitude of error reduction and robustness across different defect distributions remain uncertain.
Nonlinear interactions between defects and phonon scattering may not be fully captured by the model.
